title: PII minimization via event-sampling and retention-tier mapper
creator: Asha Raman
description: Implement a retention-tier mapper in the console analytics ingestion pipeline that minimizes the storage and surface area of PII while preserving analytical value. The mapper will classify incoming events into retention tiers (short-term raw, redacted-long-term, aggregated-only, sampled-light) using a combination of schema rules, an inline PII classifier, and deterministic sampling heuristics. It must emit metadata for traceability, drive downstream lifecycle policies, and integrate with deletion orchestration and audit attestation flows.
details: Motivation: Our analytics clusters retain a large volume of high-cardinality events containing PII that is rarely needed for product analytics but increases deletion surface and compliance risk. This work aims to reduce stored PII, make deletions faster and auditable, and provide deterministic sampled views for product telemetry without compromising legal hold or support workflows. Core components: 1) Retention-tier DSL - a small policy language that maps event types, fields, and PII scores to retention classes and TTLs. 2) Inline classifier - a lightweight, schema-aware PII detector that returns a per-event PII_score and a field-level PII mask. 3) Deterministic sampling - seeded hashing by customer_id/project_id to produce stable samples used for high-cardinality event streams. 4) Router - a low-latency step in ingestion that tags/redirects events to appropriate sinks and injects tombstone markers for short-lived tiers. 5) Backfill / reclassification tool - to re-run tier mappings for historical data. 6) Attestation and audit - append-only audit feed showing decisions for each event for compliance evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Retention-tier DSL implemented and documented in repository docs/retention-dsl.md
Inline PII classifier integrated and has configurable threshold per-team
Mapper adds <5ms p99 overhead to ingestion path under 99th percentile load
Sinks are created for 'redacted_longterm', 'aggregated_store', 'short_raw_ttl', and 'sampled_stream' with lifecycle rules applied
Backfill tool can reclassify a 30-day historical window in less than two weeks with cost estimate documented
Deletion orchestration consumes tombstone markers and results in verifiable tombstone-to-delete telemetry with audit log entries
Query-time console honors retention tags and returns redacted results for events in redacted_longterm
E2E test harness (synthetic generator + property tests) exists and runs in CI for critical flows
tasks: Design DSL and mapping defaults (privacy + PM review)
Spike lightweight PII classifier and measure latency/perf
Implement mapper function in ingestion stream (kafka consumer/ksql or ingestion lambda)
Provision sinks and lifecycle policies (S3/Lakehouse + tiered retention)
Build deterministic sampling library and integrate with mapper
Implement backfill/reclassification job and cost-estimate runbook
Add audit feed + attestation markers and wire to compliance dashboard
Integrate with deletion-orchestrator: tombstone emission and verification
Add e2e tests, load tests, and monitoring/alerts for misclassification rates
Docs, runbook, and rollout checklist with canary plan
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in sandbox with 1 customer stream for two weeks, 2) Expand to 10% of low-risk projects with aggressive monitoring, 3) Run backfill for 30-day window and validate with audit team, 4) Flip default policy to conservative minimization, then gradually tighten thresholds, 5) Full rollout with required security signoff.
metrics_and_slo: PII reduction rate (%) by event-type, ingestion latency overhead (p50/p90/p99), misclassification rate (false-positive PII, false-negative PII) measured by periodic manual sampling, time-to-delete after tombstone (median & 95th), audit-evidence completeness (% of events with attestation). Target: reduce stored PII volume by 60% for selected event types while keeping ingestion overhead <5ms p99.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overaggressive minimization removes data product teams need. Mitigation: conservative default mappings, per-project opt-out, and a rehydration path for temporarily archived raw events. Risk: Performance regression. Mitigation: optimize classifier, fallback to lightweight schema-only rules if p99 approaches threshold. Risk: Legal hold overlap. Mitigation: legal_hold check in mapper and tombstone suppression with explicit metadata and audit markers.
